entries.search: demiurges wiki demiurges is a fan-made engine for etherlords (2001) and etherlords ii (2003). it plays the games from the files of your own copy, with newly written combat, campaign, interface and rendering code that follows the original rules. this wiki explains how to set it up and how to play. demiurges contains no game content. you need your own copy of the game you want to play. the gog editions are the tested ones. getting started installing the game files: the game folder, the gog installer or a data pack. playing in the browser: nothing to install, and your files stay on your device. main menu, saves and settings: switching games and where saves are kept. playing controls: mouse, keyboard and touch. options: the original options and the remake's own settings. the adventure map: heroes, resources, buildings and turns. combat how a battle works: heroes, health, mana and spells. turn and phases: the order of a turn. attack and defence: attackers, blockers and damage. creature abilities: the most common abilities. automatic combat and the camera. encyclopedia every creature, spell, artifact, skill and specialization of both games, with its statistics and description: creatures list list sorceries and enchantments list list artifacts list list skills list list specializations list list in the game, a creature's page shows the creature itself: drag it to turn it and use the wheel to zoom. spells, creatures and heroes the four races · spells · creatures runes and artifacts · heroes and levels campaigns and modes etherlords campaigns · etherlords ii campaigns · duel about the remake differences from the originals · problems and reporting · about this wiki

entries.search: installing the game files demiurges reads the files of a game you own. it needs either game, or both: each game keeps its own rules, files and saves. nothing is downloaded for you and no game content comes with the engine. download the engine get the package for your system from the releases page, or play in the browser without installing anything. windows (x86-64) extract the zip and run demiurges.exe. smartscreen may warn about an unrecognised app: choose more info → run anyway. linux (x86-64) extract the archive and run demiurges.x86_64. if needed, run chmod +x demiurges.x86_64 first. macos extract the zip and open demiurges.app. the app is not signed: right-click it and choose open, or allow it under system settings → privacy & security. android 7+ install the apk and allow your browser or file manager to install apps when asked. add a game at the first start the game files screen opens. choose etherlords i or etherlords ii at its top, then one of: the game folder: the folder of your installed game, the one containing resources and campaigns; the gog offline installer (setup_etherlords.exe). it is not run: the engine unpacks the game files from it once and keeps them in its own data folder, so you do not need the installer afterwards; a data pack (.elpack, see below). steam copies are found automatically on windows, linux and macos: at the first start the engine uses any it finds, and the game files screen offers use the steam copy for a game not set up yet. your choice is remembered. the original start-up videos play and then the main menu opens. repeat this for the other game to keep both. data packs a data pack holds the files of one game in a single file. it is useful on a phone that has neither the installer nor the game folder: make the pack on your computer with the prepare_game_data.py script from the project (it needs python 3) and copy it to the phone: python3 prepare_game_data.py "/path/to/etherlords ii" etherlords2.elpack the installer and the data pack contain your own game files. keep them to yourself. adding, switching and removing games options › remake settings › game files… opens the same screen at any time to add a game, switch to another one or remove one. removing a game keeps its saves and settings and never deletes an installed game folder.

entries.search: playing in the browser the browser version runs at demiurges.wwworm.com. there is nothing to install: open the page, press play and give it your game files. giving it your game files choose one of: the gog offline installer (setup_etherlords.exe). it is not run: the browser unpacks the game files from it once and checks each one. this takes a few minutes and needs about 1.5 gb (etherlords) or 3 gb (etherlords ii) of browser storage; the folder of your installed game, in desktop browsers; a data pack (.elpack). repeat this for the other game to keep both. your files are never uploaded: the game reads them on your own device and keeps its copy in the browser's storage, so the next start is quick. requirements webgl 2 and a desktop-class browser, or a recent phone with plenty of memory. unpacking a large game needs a lot of memory for a short time; if it fails on a phone, use a data pack. intro and ending videos are not played in the browser yet. browsers can clear their storage. keep your installer or pack, and remember that clearing the site's data also removes your saves. this wiki the wiki you are reading is part of the same site at demiurges.wwworm.com/wiki and is also built into the game: see about this wiki.

entries.search: the adventure map between battles your heroes travel the adventure map: they visit buildings, collect resources and meet enemies. touching an enemy hero or creature starts a battle. etherlords each player has a castle. its energy is the player's life: a ruined castle is out of the game. heroes next to an enemy castle damage it every night. orders are given during the day and carried out at night. n ends the turn. resources: mandrake root, black lotus, bloody ruby, poison emerald, star sapphire, smoke diamond and frozen flames, from their glades, mines and glaciers. ether nodes give ether every turn; ether pays for global spells and the upkeep of heroes, and unused ether repairs the castle. buildings: rune shops, spell shops and creature shops of three levels that can be captured; teachers; springs such as the spring of life; merchant wagons; prisons; altars; forts; and more. five difficulty levels: easy, normal, hard, expert and impossible. etherlords ii the game runs by days; a hero can travel a limited distance each day. n ends the day. resources: plants, stones and frozen flames. buildings: spell shops, sorcerer's labs, beacons, power nodes, specialisation shrines, prisons, rune barriers and forts. crossing the pale lands costs heroes experience. the bag screen holds the hero's 16 spells, at most 4 copies of one. three difficulty levels: easy, normal and hard. saving save with the original menus or f5; load with f9. see main menu, saves and settings.

entries.search: how a battle works every battle in etherlords is a duel between two heroes, the etherlords. each hero casts spells from a spellbook: creatures fight, enchantments change the battle and sorceries act at once. the first hero whose health falls to 0 loses. demiurges follows the original rules of each game; the same structure applies to both games, with differences in the numbers. health a hero's health grows with the hero's level. the strength skill adds 10, 20 or 30%. in campaign battles the hero starts with the health they have on the map. if both heroes reach 0 at the same moment, the battle is a draw. ether and ether channels spells cost ether. each hero has ether channels, which start at 0 and grow by 0 to 2 at the start of every turn, faster for higher-level heroes. each turn the hero's ether is refilled to the number of channels, so ether you do not spend is lost. some etherlords ii spells also need a minimum number of channels, and spells with a variable cost take as much extra ether as you choose. ether disturbance stops a battle from dragging on: after a number of turns that grows with the hero's level, the hero starts losing health every turn. in etherlords the damage grows by 1 each turn; in etherlords ii it grows much faster. the channeling skill delays your own disturbance and hastens your opponent's. the hand and the spellbook both heroes start with 5 spells in hand, dealt in turn. after that, every turn starts with one draw (the side that begins does not draw on the very first turn). extra draws come from the concentration skill and some spells. at the end of your turn you keep at most 5 spells. spells are drawn at random from the spellbook, without repeats until every spell in the book has been drawn. how often a spell can be used differs between the games: see runes and artifacts. creatures a hero controls at most 10 creatures. a newly summoned creature rests: it cannot attack or use abilities that need it to rest until its owner's next turn, unless it has haste. damage on creatures heals at the end of every turn; destroyed creatures go to their owner's graveyard. see creatures and creature abilities. next turn and phases: what happens in which order. attack and defence: how attackers, blockers and damage work. spells: the three kinds of spell.

entries.search: turn and phases a turn belongs to one hero, the attacker. it has two phases: the attacker's attack/cast phase, then the opponent's block phase. then the heroes swap roles and the next turn begins. press space or the end of phase button to finish your phase. start of the turn at the start of the attacker's turn, in this order: ether disturbance damage, once it has started. healing from the regeneration skill. the attacker's creatures recover (stand up) and stop being newly summoned, except under spells that keep them down. the attacker draws a spell. ether channels grow and ether is refilled to the number of channels. enchantments that act at the start of the turn take effect. attack/cast phase the attacker casts spells and chooses which ready creatures attack. creatures that rest, were just summoned (without haste) or cannot attack stay back. berserk creatures must attack. when the attacker ends the phase, the chosen creatures attack. if no creature attacks, the block phase is skipped. block phase now the defender acts: they assign blockers (and may cast the few spells allowed in this phase) to the attacking creatures. each ready creature can block one attacker, and several creatures can block the same attacker. when the defender ends the phase, combat damage is dealt: see attack and defence. end of the turn the attacker discards down to 5 spells in hand. damage on all creatures heals. enchantments that act at the end of the turn take effect. who begins in a duel, a coin decides who attacks first in every round. in campaign battles the map decides, as in the original games. in the attack/cast phase you can cast any spell you can pay for. in the block phase only a few spells are allowed, as in the original games: polymorph, fog and energize all, and two more in etherlords ii. each card that allows it says so in its description.

entries.search: attack and defence creatures fight in the phases of a turn: the attacker chooses attackers in the attack/cast phase, the defender chooses blockers in the block phase, and then damage is dealt. who can attack a creature can attack if it is ready (not resting) and was not summoned this turn, unless it has haste. these cannot attack: creatures that cannot attack, such as walls; creatures held back by battlefield spells, for example spells that stop weak creatures; in etherlords ii, creatures in their pale aspect. berserk creatures attack whenever they can and cannot be withdrawn. a team attacker attacks only together with a creature of its own race. attacking creatures rest afterwards unless they are restless. blocking in the block phase every ready defending creature may block one attacker, and several creatures can block the same attacker, in the order you assign them. limits: only a flying creature can block a flying creature; an unblockable creature cannot be blocked; an elusive creature (etherlords ii) can only be blocked by walls. damage an unblocked attacker deals its power to the defending hero. a blocked attacker shares its power among its blockers in order, giving each as much as it needs to be destroyed before moving on to the next. every blocker strikes back with its own power. a creature with first strike hits first; if its opponent is destroyed, the opponent does not hit back. a trample attacker sends the damage left over after destroying its blockers on to the hero. damage on surviving creatures heals at the end of the turn. a hero's specialisation can add chance-based effects in combat; the hero's luck and the opponent's suppression change the odds. see creature abilities for more abilities.
entries.summary: Attackers, blockers, damage and first strike
entries.title: Attack and defence

entries.search: creature abilities abilities are shown as icons on a creature; hold the pointer over an icon for its name. the table lists the most common ones under their names in the games. numbers in brackets vary by creature. flying can be blocked only by flying creatures. cannot attack walls: they defend but never attack. first strike hits before its opponent, in attack and in defence. regeneration (1–3) when destroyed, can come back by paying the given cost. trample damage left after destroying its blockers goes to the enemy hero. lifetap damage to the enemy hero heals its owner. restless does not rest after attacking. disenchant removes the enchantments of creatures it hits. creature cannot get up does not recover by itself after resting. berserk must attack whenever it can. ether defense cannot be the target of spells or abilities. unblockable cannot be blocked. haste can act on the turn it is summoned. elusive can be blocked only by walls. team attacker attacks only together with a creature of its race. poisonous destroys a creature it damages in combat. discard (1–3) when it damages the enemy hero, the opponent discards that many random spells. pale ability, pale aspect etherlords ii: the creature can pass into its pale aspect, where it neither attacks nor is attacked. spell jamming etherlords ii: hinders the opponent's spells. many creatures also have abilities you use by resting them or paying ether; their own descriptions explain them in the game. see attack and defence for how the combat abilities work together.
entries.title: Creature abilities

entries.search: automatic combat and the camera automatic combat the auto combat button lets the computer play your side. it uses the same planning as computer opponents. press the button again to take over. if the original option for spells in automatic combat is turned off, it casts no spells or artifacts. automatic combat is not offered in hot seat duels or in the recorded combat tutorial. the battle camera drag with the right mouse button to turn the camera and use the wheel to zoom; r resets the view. on touch screens, drag with one finger and pinch to zoom. the automatic camera shows spells, the first blow of a fight and the winner in close-ups along the games' own camera tracks before returning to your view. automatic camera dynamics in options sets how often close-ups happen. moving the camera yourself ends a close-up at once. the numbers over creatures can be hidden during close-ups. watching battles again etherlords ii duels can be recorded and watched again from the duel screen.

entries.search: the four races etherlords has four races, each drawing on its own colour of ether. a race's spells share a style of play. chaots red ether of flame direct damage and aggressive creatures vitals green ether of nature strong creatures, growth and healing kinets blue ether of air flyers, tricks and control over the opponent's spells synthets black ether of the machine destruction, weakening and draining the opponent etherlords ii adds pale (colourless) spells and diamanda, the ancient creation of heroes' magic, the subject of its last campaign. pale spells fit any spellbook. races and spellbooks in a duel, a hero's spellbook must match the hero's race (pale spells are always allowed in etherlords ii). in the campaigns a hero can collect spells of any colour. see spells for the kinds of spells each race uses.
entries.title: The four races

entries.search: spells everything a hero does in battle is a spell. there are three kinds: creature summons a creature that stays until it is destroyed. see creatures. enchantment stays in play and changes a creature, a hero or the whole battlefield. sorcery acts once and is gone: damage, healing, destruction, extra spells and more. cost and casting each spell costs ether, shown on its card. some spells have a variable cost and become stronger with the extra ether you spend. a few cost health instead. you can cast spells in your attack/cast phase as long as you can pay for them and they have a target; in the block phase only a few spells are allowed. rarity spells are cantrips, common, rare or unique. cantrips are simple, unlimited spells; in etherlords a spell whose runes are used up is replaced by a cantrip of the same colour. rarer spells are more powerful and more expensive in shops and in the duel editor. artifacts some spells are artifacts: battle items with a limited number of uses. see runes and artifacts. the games' own spellbook and encyclopedia (etherlords ii) screens describe every spell. all sorceries and enchantments: etherlords · etherlords ii.
entries.title: Spells

entries.search: creatures creatures are summoned with creature spells and fight for their hero. power and toughness each creature has power, the damage it deals in combat, and toughness, the damage it can take. damage on a creature heals at the end of each turn, so a creature is destroyed only when it takes as much damage as its toughness within one turn. resting a creature that attacks or uses certain abilities rests and stays down until its owner's next turn. a newly summoned creature also rests unless it has haste. resting creatures cannot block. abilities most creatures have abilities, shown as icons. see creature abilities for the common ones and attack and defence for how they affect combat. limits a hero can control at most 10 creatures. destroyed creatures go to their owner's graveyard; some spells bring them back. all creatures: etherlords · etherlords ii.
entries.title: Creatures

entries.search: runes and artifacts runes (etherlords) in etherlords every spell in the book has runes: charges that limit how often it can be cast. when the runes of a spell are used up, a drawn copy is replaced by a random cantrip of the same colour. buy runes in rune shops and sorcerer's labs on the map; the resources skill raises how many a spell can hold. cantrips need no runes. spell charges (etherlords ii) in etherlords ii every spell in the bag starts each battle with 1, 2, 4 or 7 charges, depending on the hero's resources skill. the bag holds 16 spells, at most 4 copies of one spell. artifacts both games have artifacts: battle items with charges. an artifact can be used from a given round of the battle and then needs a number of rounds before it can be used again. a hero can use artifacts once per battle in total, or 2, 4 or 8 times with the artificer skill. in etherlords, artifacts are found on the map. in etherlords ii, heroes keep their artifacts and their charges after battle. blank artifacts can be made into new ones and spent artifacts can be recharged. see heroes and levels for the skills mentioned here. all artifacts: etherlords · etherlords ii.
entries.summary: How often spells can be used, and battle items
entries.title: Runes and artifacts

entries.search: heroes and levels heroes gain experience from battles and grow through 20 levels. each level adds health and ether income in battle. skills each new level gives a skill point and an offer of three random skills (in etherlords ii, resources is always offered first while the hero does not have it). a hero knows at most five skills, each up to rank 3. strength +10, 20 or 30% health. regeneration restores health on some turns. concentration an extra spell every few turns. channeling delays your ether disturbance and hastens the opponent's. learning more experience. luck better chances for the hero's specialisation. suppression lowers the opponent's luck. artificer more artifact uses per battle. resources more runes per spell (etherlords) or more charges per spell (etherlords ii). bargain lower shop prices (etherlords). etherlords also has skills for the map, such as mobility, estates and looting. its ethereal attack and ethereal defense have no effect, exactly as in the original game. specialisation every hero has one specialisation: a chance-based talent in battle, such as a creature dealing double damage. its chance grows with the battle's level. luck and the opponent's suppression change it. see runes and artifacts and how a battle works. all skills: etherlords · etherlords ii. all specializations: etherlords · etherlords ii.
entries.title: Heroes and levels

entries.search: etherlords campaigns etherlords has two campaigns, each played by two of the four races: flying leaf vitals and kinets flaming iron chaots and synthets start one from new game › campaign. each campaign has eight chapters. at the seventh you choose a branch, and the last chapter follows your choice. if you lose a chapter, you play it again. score your score for a chapter depends on how many days you needed compared with the expected number, and on the difficulty. the best scores are kept in the hall of fame. single missions new game › single mission plays the single missions on their own, with their own saves. see the adventure map for what happens on the map.
entries.summary: The two campaigns and the single missions
entries.title: Etherlords campaigns

entries.search: etherlords ii campaigns etherlords ii has five campaigns, played in a set order. open them from single › campaign. start with the vitals (the green ether of nature) or the chaots (the red ether of flame). the vitals campaign leads on to the synthets (the black ether of the machine), the chaots campaign to the kinets (the blue ether of air). the last campaign belongs to diamanda, the ancient creation of heroes' magic. the race campaigns have four chapters each, the last one five. the main hero, money and progress carry over between chapters. each chapter can be played at three difficulty levels. tutorial and missions single › tutorial teaches the map (adventures) and battles (combat). single › mission plays the single missions. see the adventure map and races.
entries.summary: Five campaigns, the tutorial and single missions
entries.title: Etherlords II campaigns

entries.search: duel a duel is a single battle between two heroes, outside the campaigns. open it from new game › duel (etherlords) or single › duel (etherlords ii). choosing heroes each side picks a preset: a ready-made hero with race, level, skills, specialisation, spells, runes (etherlords) and artifacts. the games' own presets are joined by those you make yourself. random picks a preset of the current resource level. the hero editor the editor changes a preset. everything costs resources, and the total must fit the chosen resource level: etherlords: resource levels 1–5, hero levels 1–15. each further copy of the same spell costs more. etherlords ii: resource levels 1–3, hero levels 1–13. the bag holds 16 spells with at most 4 copies of one. up to five skills and five artifacts. the match set the number of rounds (1–99, all of them are played) and the arena, or random for a new arena every round. a coin decides who attacks first in each round. hotseat two players can play on one computer (hotseat). a message between turns tells the next player to take the seat. network play is not available. replays etherlords ii duels can be saved and watched again (replay on the duel screen). the engine reads the original replays and writes its own. see how a battle works.
entries.summary: Presets, the hero editor, hot seat and replays
entries.title: Duel

entries.search: differences from the originals demiurges follows the rules of the original games. it runs on modern systems and changes only what this page lists. added both games in one program, switched from the main menu, each with its own rules, saves and settings. windows, linux, macos, android and the browser; touch controls. remake settings: soft shadows, terrain detail, sharpening, anti-aliasing and more. the automatic camera can be interrupted by moving the camera yourself. this wiki, in english and russian, in the game and on the web. not available network play. local hot seat duels work. loading saves of the original games. original etherlords ii replays can be watched. intro and ending videos in the browser. not yet exact computer opponents follow the original's approach but are not an exact copy of its decisions. the darkening of a few large spells, the timing of some ability effects and etherlords ii map particles are approximations. a few rare messages are still in english. kept on purpose some behaviour of the originals looks like a mistake but is kept because the games work that way: the etherlords skills ethereal attack and ethereal defense do nothing. random battle events of etherlords never happen, as in the original. several etherlords global spells only cost upkeep. as in the originals, computer players never answer alliance or trade offers. see problems and reporting for known gaps.
entries.summary: What the remake adds, leaves out and keeps on purpose
entries.title: Differences from the originals

entries.search: problems and reporting demiurges is still in development. these are the things you are most likely to notice. known gaps a few rare messages are still shown in english, mostly in the duel editor and in error messages. computer opponents follow the original's approach but do not copy its decisions exactly. as in the original, they never answer alliance or trade offers. the campaigns are tested screen by screen and system by system, not yet by playing every chapter from start to finish. there is no network multiplayer. local hot seat duels work. touch controls have only been tried in testing, not yet on many real phones. the interface keeps the original layout, so on a small phone text and buttons are small. intro and ending videos are not played in the browser yet. if the game does not start check that you chose the folder that contains resources and campaigns, or the gog offline installer. see installing the game files. in the browser, make sure the page has enough storage and memory; on a phone, try a data pack. on windows and macos, allow the unsigned app as described in installing the game files. reporting a problem report problems on the issues page. say which game and which system you use, and what you did before the problem appeared.

entries.search: about this wiki the wiki is available in two places with the same articles: in the game: the wiki button on the main menu and on the game files screen, the wiki button under the etherlords ii esc menus in battle and on the map, or f1 on any screen. the game waits while you read; esc, f1 or close returns to it; on the web at demiurges.wwworm.com/wiki, free to read without game files, an account or the engine. the browser version's start page links to it. languages every article is written in english and russian. switch with en / ru at the top of the in-game wiki or with the language list on the website. your choice is remembered. until you choose, the in-game wiki follows the language of your game's texts and the website follows your browser. names of game things (races, phases, menus) follow the original games' own english and russian texts where they apply. what it covers the guides explain how to play the games on this engine and how the engine differs from the originals. the encyclopedia has a page for every creature, sorcery, enchantment, artifact, skill and specialization of both games, with its statistics, prices and description. on the website, creature pages show a picture of the creature; in the game they show the creature itself, which you can turn and zoom. the encyclopedia in the game is built from your own copy, so it follows your game's language and data. the website's encyclopedia was exported from the original russian and english (gog) editions. names, descriptions and pictures of the games' content belong to their owners.
